reviews.text: Hey, Dima K. here =) Good job, guys. Nice game. Continue working on it, looks very promising. Full support from me. For people who actually read review: The game is WIP, (well duh), rough around the edges and etc., but the gameplay is still very fun. Makes your brains work. Plus the devs actually read reviews and ideas in community hub and discord. A lot of day-one issues were already fixed.

Just what I was looking for! I’m having a blast with this game. Every run feels fresh as I try out new upgrades and strategies, and the atmosphere pulls me right in. The art style is unique and sets such a great mood. The shops are a really fun addition. I can’t wait to keep exploring and see what else the game has in store!
Moved a pawn, triggered a trap, lost half my team, and the board started shifting like it was possessed. 10/10, would get checkmated by a hallway again.

Awsome game! Interesting twist on chess, adding this magical world around it makes it feel like an adventure. Also power ups, Bosses and other elements from more action based genres makes it feel intense and challenging. I only lost to the boss twice so far, but I enjoyed my time in this world and I wait to see what the game will become on launch. Still I imagine there is a way to go but for what I've seen so far it looks very promising!

So lucky to have gotten a key for this - the game is top tier for sure! Love the combination between roguelite and plain-old chess, and the Hades-style narrative just makes it all the better! I highly recommend it to anyone who wants to oil up their brain gears a bit, you can't afford to lose attention on the field here. Prepare to die a lot, this game is as tough as nails (ahem ahem f*ck Pawnathan ahem ahem) The art direction, the animations, and SFX and VFX - all look phenomenal - way to go!!!

Overall? It's pretty good. I'd give it a 6/10 on it's own, but a 7.5/10 among early access games. As of today (08/31/2025) It's very clearly unfinished, but it has lots of potential, and a fairly well executed gimmick. [h3] The Good: [/h3] - Good Core Mechanics Each piece is unique in it's capabilities and 'vibe'. You can choose a certain play-style depending on how you prefer to move around the levels. i.e.: Which chess piece you're most comfortable with, for me this was the almighty pony. The shops, upgrade vendors, and encounters felt good to progress through and interact with. Solid foundation. - Killer Sound Track But with the caveat that there should be more diversity. It's a good start, but needs more meat on the bones, so to speak. The sound design in general is serviceable. Not fantastic, but definitely not bad. Repetitive sounds are present, but not overbearing. - Consistent Theme With gameplay becoming increasingly complex and difficult as you go through floors I never felt drawn out of the experience by something jarring or incongruent. I believe the animations and drawn cutscenes contribute a lot to the charm and identity of this game. All these things together make for a great experience. - Good Gameplay The clicking and moving of pieces is tight, responsive, and satisfying. I don't think I've ever encountered a bug playing as intended in this way. - Good meta-progression. I love me some meta-progression in rougelikes, this feels very much like Hades' Mirror of Darkness, and the accompanying keepsakes were mashed together, in a good way. [h3] The Bad: [/h3] - Very seldom are things made clear to the player. I found myself saying "What is that?" or "What did that do?" frequently while playing. I understand that games, and especially rougelikes are more fun when experienced for oneself, and discovering things as you play is part of the charm, but there were multiple, repeatable instances of me finding something new or picking something up and I had 0 idea what had just happened and seemingly no way to check aftert the fact. More tooltips would be welcome, and maybe a way to see what happened in a previous turn. [h3] Spoilers Within This Paragraph [/h3] [spoiler] Specifically, on the first boss it is not made clear to the player what the boss is/can do other than visual cues which is fine, but can feel unfair. The boss will also debuff any piece that touches it, which would also be fine if the only ways to tell a piece was debuffed was not a very small indicator next to the piece and the new power value on the piece's portrait. Granted, if you hover over the small icon indicating [i] something [/i] was going on with your piece, it would explain the debuff, but I feel like this could be made more obvious. [/spoiler] There was a recurring feeling of the game failing to communicate important information to me. And this can make for some frustrating and [i] seemingly [/i] unfair deaths, which is something to be avoided in a rougelike in my opinion. - No en passant? I love chess, but I never felt that my knowledge of the game helped in any way while playing. There is little correlation other than the pieces moving in the same way (except the pawn which can move backwards). You are given precious few pieces, so any strategy involving trading pieces is immediately nonviable. The opponent is allowed to move every one of their pieces in a single turn, while you are only allowed to move one piece. This disallows any discovered attacks, threatening moves, recaptures, or really any form of strategy beyond straight-up material gain. This is alleviated somewhat by the abilities you can unlock and use, but the lack of follow through with the idea was disappointing. - Replayability Even with my small amount of time playing, I found myself memorizing encounters. The bosses, specifically are very static and unchanging, if you know a way past, it will work every time. I feel like it could get stale without more randomization or something else to spice runs up and help differentiate them. I feel like these are the most important points, but above all I did have fun playing, and will continue to play this and follow the development.

I think its important for people to understand that more then this game is a chess rogue-like, its a chess **themed** rogue-like. and thats a critical distinction. yes, while its true that the core "unit" movement works like traditional chess, on a macro level it plays similer to games like Into The Breach. and so, even though there are some kinks that need to be ironed out, if you like tactical games that require you to put in a lot of thought before each action you take - then I highly reccomand giving this game a shot.

This game deserves more love. I don't play chess often. I know how to play, but I barley have over 700 elo on chess.com. Despite my lack of skill, I still find this game super enjoyable! It has satisfying animations, appealing visuals, and is overall super easy to play! You don't need to be some chess grandmaster to enjoy the game, and that is one of the best features. The story is entertaining, most of the pieces have a unique personality, and the music matches the theme very well. Overall, this game deserves a much larger community because this game is better than over half the games EA is developing these days. If you are thinking about buying this game, just do it. It's super cheap and if you don't like it, you can just issue a refund. At least give this game a chance.
棋子有血量和攻击力，更类似战棋+解谜，可以买一次性道具、技能，技能还可以升级，每次战斗地形、敌人、障碍物、宝箱、特殊门之类都是随机的，甚至可以退出重进刷新。还是挺有趣的，之前B站上传过试玩视频，主要是很喜欢国际象棋，沾边的游戏都想试试，打折21挺值得，希望正式版能再多加点内容，单词虽然不复杂，有中文会更好增加销量一点吧，也想要创意工坊

I should state that I have not read any patch notes so I have no clue if any of my issues are getting fixed but at this moment I have some issues. 1. As far as I'm aware there is no undo button, I know that the game shouldn't baby me all the time but an easy mode that has an undo button would be nice especially when my pieces die due to a game mechanic I didn't understand. For example I pulled a rook with the hook ability over an ice tile and it killed my piece and ended my run when I assumed the rook would have just sat on top of the ice tile. 2. In the same run just before losing I only had a bishop left and if I did not have the hook ability I would have been soft locked because of my pieces limited mobility, the push tiles placement, and the ice tiles. This is my only experience with a potential soft lock so I have no idea if there is already an anti soft lock mechanic. 3. Bosses feel impossible without cheesing, I have only beat a mini boss and a normal boss once but both times I had to use a bishop to cheese the pawns movement. Every other time I fought a boss all my pieces would die because they get pushed off the map or because of my pieces limited movement. I know it's chess but as someone who enjoys roguelikes but does not enjoy chess very much I would rather not have to plan 10+ moves ahead just to get a single hit on a boss with 8 health and have no movement to get out of the way of the bosses next turn when it can move 3 tiles and I can only move one. 4. The hook ability feels incredibly broken compared to almost every other ability I've read, especially at max level. (I haven't gotten that far into the game) 5. It feels really hard to keep track of which tiles will get my pieces killed because white just has so many pieces compared to me and all the holes and obstacles in the map really limit my movement. These are the only complaints I can think of right now, Im gonna take a break from the game until the next update but I have high hopes most of the issues will be fixed soon. (Yes I know some of my complaints is just a skill issue.)

It was a great game, but somehow its even more buggy on release than it was in early access. Visuals will stay on certain abilities and completely cover areas, sometimes you can see full patrol rotations of the white pieces, but its completely random when you can and can't see them, loading into a new room you will sometimes be completely unable to place pieces and have to fully exit the game and reload it to fix the issue.
Amazing Idea, since full release too buggy to play it was actually better in early access somehow? Will come Back to check if it is fixed sometime,

EDIT: Thanks to another reviewer, it seems this game is no longer in hands of original developers. It was released in an incomplete state, thus why only two floors and an assortment of bugs. Unless this comes back to original developers, DO NOT BUY! Original: At this time, I would not recommend buying this game until the bugs are resolved. Currently, it requires a lot of restarts or avoiding certain areas to play the game. OTHER THAN THE BUGS, it is a great concept, intriguing gameplay, basic but inoffensive story, interesting mechanics, and wonderful artstyle, There is great ideas wrapped in Chess mechanics making it a puzzle roguelike game. The bugs are very infuriating though. I so far have only been able to complete up to the 2nd floor and then the game resets. I've completed multiple runs but I haven't gotten any more story after unlocking the ability to sculpt. I do not think this game is complete yet, or if it is, requires way more grinding than I thought since I stopped getting stories after more than 4-6 victories.

Announcement Post from the official discord of the game: Nettart — 5/6/2026 12:11 PMWednesday, May 6, 2026 12:11 PM Hey @everyone I’m sorry for the long silence. It’s been a difficult time, and unfortunately, I have some tough news to share. Last month, the company under which we developed Once a Pawn a King (and which still owns the IP) let go of its workers - ourselves included. We’re still doing what we can to fix bugs and make small improvements, but as things stand right now, the game is no longer in our hands. Once a Pawn a King is set to fully release in about a week, in a very unfinished state. There will be some new features and dialogue, but there won’t be a third floor, and the King will remain eternally missing. We are currently exploring the possibility of buying back the IP from our previous employer, but due to existing agreements with a publisher, the situation is complicated. I’m truly sorry to share this news. Your support has meant the world to us, and the community we started to build around this game is something we’re incredibly grateful for. From the entire Perrenormal team - thank you. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The owners that fired the dev team are doing nothing to fix the game and pushed a 1.0 release that crashes constantly, and have made no indication that they are doing anything to fix it; they do not respond to request tickets/posts. This game would be good if fixed and polished instead of the team that made it getting canned over financial B.S.

The full release is a buggy mess. It felt far more user friendly and playable before 1.0. A list of the bugs i've encountered so far for 1.0 Health/Damage overlays stay and block visuals after a piece has been captured. Paths don't show when they should, and are sometimes shown permanantly after a capture. Only 2 floors. Definently only half finished. Consistent crashes. No cue on how to progress the story or gain unlockable resources (memories). Re-rolls on shops sometimes just don't work. Furniture blocks the view of the 'catapault' tiles, meaning you can't see the direction those tiles will move you. Cursor over on some squares for selection is incredibly precise, particularly when using blessings. The Figure that unlocks a purified curse for all pieces, doesn't give them to you purified. The premise of this game is really cool, I like the Slay The Spire-esque setup, the idea of the chess pieces working to free their king and progress a story is fun. But the game is a buggy mess.... shame, because the early access showed a lot of promise.
I love the concept and story but Gods the bugs are annoying, and everything feels so slow
